title: Ivory and Wheat
story: Three tiers finished in a buttercream left deliberately unsmoothed, with wheat cut that morning from the field behind the barn.

image.alt: A three tier ivory wedding cake dressed with stems of wheat

title: The Quiet Tier
story: Two tiers for sixty people who wanted no flowers at all, so the surface does the work instead.

image.alt: A two tier white wedding cake with a plain swept surface

title: Olive and Salt
story: Olive oil sponge for a windy cliff top, because butter sets hard and olive oil does not.

image.alt: A single tier olive oil cake on a table with the sea behind it

title: Forty, Loudly
story: Passionfruit and coconut for someone who asked for the brightest thing I could make in February.

image.alt: A bright coconut and passionfruit birthday cake with toasted flakes

title: Chocolate for Iris
story: A seventh birthday, and the only brief was that it had to be so dark it looked like soil.

image.alt: A very dark chocolate birthday cake with a single candle

title: Nine Candles
story: Strawberries folded through the buttercream so the whole thing went faintly pink on its own.

image.alt: A pale pink strawberry cake with nine thin candles

title: The Letter Cake
story: The brief arrived as a handwritten letter, and the piping copies the sender's own hand from it.

image.alt: A cake piped with handwriting across the top surface

title: Blue Hour
story: Buttercream mixed in nine shades and blended on the cake itself, working from the base upward.

image.alt: A cake finished in blended blue buttercream shading from dark to pale

title: Grandmother's Tin
story: Baked in the client's grandmother's own tin, which she brought to the studio wrapped in a tea towel.

image.alt: A square cake baked in an old family tin, still in the tin

title: Rhubarb, Forced
story: Made in the three weeks when forced rhubarb is that impossible pink, and not one week either side.

image.alt: A cake topped with poached pink rhubarb batons

title: Late Figs
story: The last crate of the year, roasted with honey until they gave up and collapsed.

image.alt: An Earl Grey cake crowned with roasted figs

title: Quince in November
story: Quince poached for four hours until it turned the colour of old brick, then laid in a single overlapping ring.

image.alt: A cake ringed with slices of deep amber poached quince
